summary: Anschütz and Le Bras classify p-divisible groups over a quasi-syntomic ring by prismatic linear algebra. For a p-divisible group G over a quasi-syntomic ring R they define M_Δ(G) = Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris), the Ext of abelian sheaves on the small quasi-syntomic site of R with values in the pushforward O^pris = v_*O_Δ of the prismatic structure sheaf, with the Frobenius induced by that of O^pris. Their first theorem is that this pair is an admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystal — a finite locally free O^pris-module whose linearized Frobenius has cokernel killed by the prism ideal, and whose Frobenius image in M/I^pris·M is a finite locally free module over the structure sheaf injecting after base change — of rank the height of G, with M_Δ(G)/Fil ≅ Lie(Ǧ). Their main theorem is that M_Δ is an antiequivalence between p-divisible groups over R and admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R. The proof descends to quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings, where crystals are modules over the initial prism Δ_R and admissibility becomes a window structure over the Nygaard frame; full faithfulness comes from recovering T_pǦ as ker(φ/ξ̃ − 1) on the first Nygaard piece, using Bhatt–Lurie's computation of the Frobenius fixed points; essential surjectivity is proved by deforming along surjections on whose kernel the divided Frobenius is topologically nilpotent, down to the perfectoid case, which is Lau's and Scholze–Weinstein's theorem. Section 5 adds the classification of finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over a perfectoid ring by torsion prismatic Dieudonné modules, the recovery of the Breuil–Kisin classification over a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field together with the identification of the prismatic functor with Kisin's, the functor to Zink's displays with an antiequivalence between formal p-divisible groups and F-nilpotent displays, and the étale comparison recovering the generic-fibre Tate module. The atlas plans the whole prismatic apparatus the paper uses — δ-rings, prisms, prismatic envelopes and the perfect-prism/perfectoid equivalence at PrismaticCohomology PR.0, the relative site with the Hodge–Tate and crystalline comparisons at PR.1, derived prismatic cohomology and the quasi-regular semiperfectoid calculation at PR.2, the Nygaard filtration with its divided Frobenius and Breuil–Kisin twists at PR.3, the étale comparison at PR.4, the absolute site at PR.5 and prismatic F-crystals at PR.7, with perfectoid rings and André's lemma at PerfectoidQuotients Q0 and Q3, the quasi-syntomic site at DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 and DD.5, and p-divisible groups, classical Dieudonné theory and Breuil–Kisin modules at FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1, R07.2 and R07.4. What it plans nowhere is the Dieudonné theory itself: the morphism of topoi to the quasi-syntomic site, the sheaves O^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris and I^pris, prismatic Dieudonné crystals and modules with admissibility, frames, windows and displays, the functor M_Δ and its comparisons, and the classification theorems. Those are routed as a Part II of PrismaticCohomology; the paper's prism and prismatic-cohomology generalities are routed as sources of PR.0 to PR.3, and six further statements as sources of PerfectoidQuotients Q0, PerfectoidSpaces P7, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1, AInfCohomology AI.2 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4.

items.name: Filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystal
items.statement: A filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystal over a quasi-syntomic ring R is a triple (M, Fil M, φ_M) consisting of a finite locally free O^pris-module M, an O^pris-submodule Fil M and a φ-linear map φ_M : M → M such that (1) φ_M(Fil M) ⊆ I^pris·M; (2) N^{≥1}O^pris·M ⊆ Fil M and M/Fil M is a finite locally free O-module; (3) φ_M(Fil M) generates I^pris·M as an O^pris-module. The category of these is denoted DF(R). The forgetful functor DF(R) → DM(R) is fully faithful with essential image the admissible objects.
items.note: This was the formulation of the main objects in the earlier versions of the paper; the referee's observation that DF(R) embeds fully faithfully into DM(R) with image the admissible crystals is what allowed the authors to work with admissibility instead. Nothing in the atlas plans either notion. The Part II must carry both, because the filtered form is what Remark 5.7 (arXiv Remark 5.1.8) uses to state the obstruction for finite locally free group schemes over a general quasi-syntomic ring.

items.name: Rank and Lie algebra of the prismatic Dieudonné crystal
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G over a quasi-syntomic ring R, the rank of the finite locally free O^pris-module M_Δ(G) is the height of G, and the quotient M_Δ(G)/φ_{M_Δ(G)}^{-1}(I^pris·M_Δ(G)) is naturally isomorphic to Lie(Ǧ), where Ǧ is the Cartier dual of G.
items.note: The rank statement is proved as part of Proposition 4.69 (arXiv Proposition 4.6.5) and the identification of the quotient with Lie(Ǧ) as part of Theorem 4.71 (arXiv Theorem 4.6.7); it is stated as a separate result in the introduction and is the numerical content of the classification, so it is an item of its own.

items.name: Antiequivalence of the crystalline Dieudonné functor in characteristic p
items.statement: As a corollary of the main theorem and of the comparison with the crystalline Dieudonné functor: for a quasi-syntomic ring R with pR = 0, the contravariant Dieudonné functor of crystalline Dieudonné theory is an antiequivalence between p-divisible groups over R and the corresponding category of crystalline Dieudonné crystals. For excellent l.c.i. rings full faithfulness was proved by de Jong and Messing, and the antiequivalence by Lau for F-finite l.c.i. rings.
items.note: A stated corollary of Theorem 1.16 (arXiv Theorem 1.4.4) together with Theorem 4.46 (arXiv Theorem 4.3.2). FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans classical Dieudonné theory over perfect residue fields only, and no layer plans crystalline Dieudonné theory over a general quasi-syntomic F_p-algebra.

items.name: Admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules over a perfectoid ring are minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
items.statement: If R is a perfectoid ring, admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals (equivalently modules) over R are equivalent to minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules for R in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze. Consequently the main theorem contains as a special case the results of Lau and of Scholze–Weinstein; but the proof of the main theorem requires that special case as an input (in fact only the case of perfectoid valuation rings with algebraically closed and spherically complete fraction field is needed).
items.note: AInfCohomology AI.2 builds Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules, their lattices and modifications from BMS1, but not the minuscule condition nor its identification with prismatic Dieudonné modules; that identification is the dictionary that lets this paper cite Lau and Scholze–Weinstein, so the paper is a source for AI.2.

items.name: δ-ring
items.statement: A δ-ring is a pair (A, δ) with A a commutative ring and δ : A → A a map of sets such that δ(0) = δ(1) = 0, δ(xy) = x^p δ(y) + y^p δ(x) + p δ(x) δ(y) and δ(x+y) = δ(x) + δ(y) + (x^p + y^p − (x+y)^p)/p for all x, y ∈ A. A morphism of δ-rings f : (A,δ) → (A′,δ′) is a ring morphism with f ∘ δ = δ′ ∘ f. Writing φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x) gives a lift of Frobenius, and this is an equivalence of structures when A is p-torsion free.
items.note: PR.0 constructs p-derivations and δ-rings, free δ-algebras and Frobenius lifts, and proves their equivalence with a lift of Frobenius only in p-torsion-free rings.

items.name: Free δ-rings, limits and colimits
items.statement: The category of δ-rings has all limits and colimits and they are computed on the underlying rings. In particular free δ-rings exist: for a δ-ring A and a set X, the free δ-ring A{X} on X is the polynomial ring over A on the variables δ^n(x) for n ≥ 0 and x ∈ X. The Frobenius on Z_(p){X} is faithfully flat.
items.note: PR.0 constructs free δ-algebras and their flatness properties; the warning attached to the footnote — that this fails for rings with a Frobenius lift in the presence of p-torsion — is exactly PR.0's stated caveat.

items.name: Elements of rank one and distinguished elements
items.statement: Let (A, δ) be a δ-ring. An element x ∈ A is of rank 1 if δ(x) = 0. An element d ∈ A is distinguished if δ(d) ∈ A^× is a unit.
items.note: PR.0 constructs distinguished elements and orientations.

items.name: p-power roots give elements of rank one
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and x ∈ A. Then δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A for all n. In particular, if A is p-adically separated and y ∈ A admits a p^n-th root for all n ≥ 0, then δ(y) = 0, i.e. y has rank 1.
items.note: Part of PR.0's δ-ring calculus; it is the lemma that makes Teichmüller-type elements of a perfectoid ring have rank one, which PR.0 needs for the perfect prism/perfectoid correspondence.

items.name: Prism; bounded prism
items.statement: A δ-pair (A, I) is a prism if I ⊆ A is an invertible ideal such that A is derived (p, I)-complete and p ∈ I + φ(I)A. A prism (A, I) is bounded if A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion.
items.note: PR.0 constructs prisms with exactly these conditions and insists that I be an effective Cartier divisor, that A be derived (p,I)-complete and that p lie in I + φ(I)A, and that boundedness mean bounded p-power torsion in A/I.

items.name: Basic properties of prisms
items.statement: (1) The condition p ∈ I + φ(I)A is equivalent to I being pro-Zariski locally on Spec(A) generated by a distinguished element; for a perfect prism it is automatic. (2) If (A,I) → (B,J) is a morphism of prisms, i.e. a δ-ring map carrying I into J, then J = IB. (3) (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) with [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) is a prism. (4) If (A,I) is bounded then A is classically (p,I)-adically complete, hence p-adically separated.
items.note: PR.0 proves the rigidity I·B = J for a prism map, the local principality of I and the classical completeness of a bounded prism, and takes (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) with φ(q) = q^p as one of its acceptance examples, noting that the q-prism ideal is [p]_q and not q − 1.

items.name: Regular sequences in a transversal prism
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and let d ∈ I be distinguished. If (p, d) is a regular sequence in A, then for all r, s ≥ 0 with r ≠ s the sequences (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) are regular.
items.note: Pure prism algebra, proved here and used in Section 4.9; PR.0 owns δ-ring and prism regularity statements but does not name it, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Perfect prisms are the same as integral perfectoid rings
items.statement: The functor {perfect prisms (A,I)} → {integral perfectoid rings R}, (A,I) ↦ A/I, is an equivalence of categories, with inverse R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker(θ̃)), where A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{-1} with θ Fontaine's theta map. A prism is perfect if the Frobenius on the underlying δ-ring is an isomorphism. In particular the ideal I of a perfect prism is principal.
items.note: PR.0 proves precisely this equivalence, using the integral perfectoid/tilt/A_inf construction supplied by PerfectoidQuotients Q0's integral-algebra prefix, and states that it is a theorem and not a definition. Mathlib has Witt vectors, the tilt (PreTilt, Perfection) and Fontaine's theta map (WittVector.fontaineTheta), but no perfectoid rings and no δ-rings, so the statement itself is not in the libraries.

items.name: Perfectoidness of étale extensions and of henselizations
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring and let R → R′ be p-completely étale. Then R′ is perfectoid. Moreover, if J ⊆ R is an ideal, then the p-completion R′ of the henselization of R at J is perfectoid.
items.note: Q0's integral-algebra prefix owns integral perfectoid rings and their stability properties; the henselization statement is proved here and is used in Section 4.6 to lift p-divisible groups, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: A perfect prism is initial
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism. Then for every prism (B, J) the map Hom((A,I),(B,J)) → Hom(A/I, B/J) is a bijection.
items.note: This is the universal property that makes (A_inf(R), ker θ̃) the initial object of the prismatic site of a perfectoid ring R; PR.0 constructs maps of prisms and proves the perfect-prism/perfectoid equivalence in the Bhatt–Scholze §3 range that contains it.

items.name: Nygaard filtration of a prism
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism. Set N^{≥i}A := φ^{-1}(I^i) for i ≥ 0. The filtration N^{≥•}A is the Nygaard filtration of (A, I).
items.note: PR.3 constructs the Nygaard pieces by the actual Frobenius-divisibility condition and the divided Frobenius, which is this definition.

items.name: Convergence of the q-logarithm
items.statement: Let (B, J) be a prism over (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)). Then for every element x ∈ 1 + N^{≥1}B of rank 1, i.e. with δ(x) = 0, the series log_q(x) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1} q^{−n(n−1)/2} (x−1)(x−q)⋯(x−q^{n−1})/[n]_q is well defined and converges in B. Moreover log_q(x) ∈ N^{≥1}B and, in B[1/p][[x−1]]^{∧(q−1)}, one has log_q(x) = ((q−1)/log q)·log(x) with log(x) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1}(x−1)^n/n.
items.note: The q-logarithm is constructed here for the computation of the prismatic Dieudonné module of μ_{p^∞}. PrismaticCohomology PR.6 plans q-crystalline charts and the AΩ comparison but not the q-logarithm; since the only use in this paper is inside the Dieudonné theory, it is routed to the Part II, and a reviewer who prefers to give the q-de Rham layer ownership of it should move it to PR.6.

items.name: The divided q-logarithm
items.statement: Let (B, J) be a bounded prism over (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) and let x ∈ Z_p(1)(B/J). Then [x^{1/p}]_{θ̃} ∈ B has rank 1 and lies in 1 + N^{≥1}B, so that log_q([x^{1/p}]_{θ̃}) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1} q^{−n(n−1)/2} ([x^{1/p}]_{θ̃}−1)⋯([x^{1/p}]_{θ̃}−q^{n−1})/[n]_q exists in B.
items.note: The form of the q-logarithm actually used: it produces the element ℓ_q that trivialises the Breuil–Kisin twist and computes the prismatic Dieudonné functor on Hom(Q_p/Z_p, μ_{p^∞}).

items.name: Relative prismatic site
items.statement: For a bounded prism (A, I) and a p-complete A/I-algebra R, the prismatic site of R relative to A, denoted (R/A)_Δ, is the category whose objects are bounded prisms (B, IB) over (A, I) together with an A/I-algebra map R → B/IB, with the obvious morphisms, endowed with the Grothendieck topology whose covers are the (p,I)-completely faithfully flat morphisms of prisms over (A, I).
items.note: PR.1 constructs the relative prismatic site with its complete faithfully flat covers, its structure sheaf and its reduced structure sheaf.

items.name: Set-theoretic cut-off for the prismatic site
items.statement: A cut-off cardinal κ is fixed and all objects of the prismatic site are assumed of cardinality < κ, so that presheaves on (R/A)_Δ and on (R)_Δ admit sheafification. The results do not change when κ is enlarged: prismatic cohomology can be computed by a Čech–Alexander complex, and the categories of prismatic Dieudonné crystals are independent of κ.
items.note: PR.1 constructs Čech–Alexander envelope models and hyperdescent, which is the mechanism by which independence of the cut-off is proved; the size discipline itself is part of the site construction there.

items.name: The prismatic structure sheaves
items.statement: The functor O_Δ (resp. Ō_Δ) on the prismatic site, valued in (p,I)-complete δ-A-algebras (resp. in p-complete R-algebras), sending (B, IB) ∈ (R/A)_Δ to B (resp. to B/IB), is a sheaf. It is called the prismatic structure sheaf (resp. the reduced prismatic structure sheaf).
items.locator: arXiv:1907.10525v4 (11 October 2022), Proposition 3.1.3 (published: Proposition 3.3); attributed there to Bhatt–Scholze, Corollary 3.12
items.note: PR.1 constructs the structure sheaf and reduced structure sheaf on the relative site and proves the sheaf property.

items.name: Absolute prismatic site
items.statement: For a p-complete ring R, the absolute prismatic site (R)_Δ is the category whose objects are bounded prisms (B, J) together with a ring map R → B/J, with the obvious morphisms, endowed with the Grothendieck topology whose covers are the morphisms of prisms (B, J) → (C, JC) that are (p,J)-completely faithfully flat.
items.note: PR.5 constructs the absolute prismatic site of a p-adic formal scheme, its structure and prism-ideal sheaves, and its comparison with the relative sites.

items.name: Prismatic and Hodge–Tate complexes of a smooth algebra
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. The prismatic complex is Δ_{R/A} = RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ), a (p,I)-complete commutative algebra object of D(A) with a semilinear φ induced by the Frobenius of O_Δ. The reduced or Hodge–Tate complex is Δ̄_{R/A} = RΓ((R/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ), a p-complete commutative algebra object of D(R).
items.note: PR.1 constructs the Frobenius on derived global sections over the relative site and proves coordinate independence.

items.name: Hodge–Tate comparison
items.statement: For R p-completely smooth over A/I, the map η extends to a map η_R^* : (Ω^•_{R/(A/I)}{}^{∧p}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}), β_I) which is an isomorphism, where β_I is the Bockstein differential.
items.locator: arXiv:1907.10525v4 (11 October 2022), Theorem 3.1.6 (published: Theorem 3.6); attributed there to Bhatt–Scholze, Theorem 4.10
items.note: PR.1 proves the Hodge–Tate comparison on affines, H^i(Δ ⊗^L_A A/I) ≅ Ω^i with twist (I/I²)^{−i}, together with its multiplicative map and the Bockstein differential; this is its source, Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 4.10.

items.name: Crystalline comparison
items.statement: Under the same assumptions, and for a prism with I = (p), there is a canonical isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), compatible with Frobenius, where R^{(1)} is the Frobenius twist.
items.locator: arXiv:1907.10525v4 (11 October 2022), Theorem 3.1.7 (published: Theorem 3.7); attributed there to Bhatt–Scholze, Theorem 5.2
items.note: PR.1 proves the crystalline comparison for I = (p) using CR.2's PD Poincaré lemma, with the φ_A-twisted scalar extension; this is its source, Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2.

items.name: Crystalline comparison for syntomic and quasi-syntomic algebras
items.statement: The proof of the crystalline comparison goes through for a syntomic A/J-algebra R: in the Čech–Alexander proof the kernel of B^• → R̃ is in each simplicial degree the inductive limit of ideals (p, x_1, …, x_r) with (x_1, …, x_r) p-completely regular relative to A. The statement then extends by descent from the quasi-regular semiperfect case to all quasi-syntomic F_p-algebras.
items.note: The extension of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2 beyond the smooth case is proved here and is what makes the comparison with crystalline Dieudonné theory possible; PR.1 owns the crystalline comparison and PR.2 the descent from quasi-regular semiperfect rings, so the paper is a source for those layers.

items.name: Derived prismatic and derived Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: The derived prismatic cohomology functor LΔ_{−/A} (resp. the derived Hodge–Tate functor LΔ̄_{−/A}) is the left Kan extension of Δ_{−/A} (resp. Δ̄_{−/A}) from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras to the category of p-complete A/I-algebras, valued in (p,I)-complete commutative algebra objects of D(A) (resp. p-complete commutative algebra objects of D(R)).
items.note: PR.2 extends the smooth-algebra functor by the coherent left Kan extension of Bhatt–Scholze Construction 7.6 and derived completion, and proves independence.

items.name: Conjugate filtration on derived Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: For any p-complete A/I-algebra R, the derived Hodge–Tate complex Δ̄_{R/A} carries a functorial increasing multiplicative exhaustive filtration Fil_*^conj in p-complete objects of D(R), with canonical identifications gr_i^conj(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≃ (∧^i L_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i])^{∧p}.
items.note: PR.2 proves the filtered derived Hodge–Tate comparison with exterior powers of the completed cotangent complex.

items.name: Prismatic cohomology of a p-adic formal scheme
items.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme over Spf(A/I) which is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion. There is a functorially defined (p,I)-complete commutative algebra object Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X, A) with a φ_A-linear map φ_X, such that RΓ(U, Δ_{X/A}) ≅ Δ_{R/A} compatibly with Frobenius for every affine open U = Spf(R), and such that Δ̄_{X/A} = Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I carries a functorial increasing multiplicative exhaustive filtration Fil_*^conj with gr_i^conj(Δ̄_{X/A}) ≃ (∧^i L_{X/(A/I)}{−i}[−i])^{∧p}.
items.note: The globalisation of the relative theory of PR.1 and of the derived theory and its conjugate filtration in PR.2.

items.name: The first conjugate piece is the cotangent complex over the prism
items.statement: For X as above there is a canonical isomorphism α_X : (L_{X/Spf(A)}{−1}[−1])^{∧p} ≅ Fil_1^conj(Δ̄_{X/A}), where the right-hand side is the first piece of the increasing conjugate filtration.
items.note: This refines PR.2's conjugate filtration: the cotangent complex is taken relative to Spf(A), not to A/I, so the extension of O_X by L{−1}[−1] is split off canonically. It is proved here (the authors thank Bhargav Bhatt for a discussion about this section) and is used to detect liftings; PR.2 owns the conjugate filtration, so the paper is a source for it.

items.name: Obstruction class for lifting a flat scheme
items.statement: Let S be a ring, I ⊆ S an invertible ideal and X a flat S̄ := S/I-scheme. Then the class γ ∈ Ext²_{O_X}(L_{X/Spec(S̄)}, I/I² ⊗_{S̄} O_X) defined by L_{X/Spec(S)} is ± the obstruction class for lifting X to a flat S/I²-scheme.
items.note: Illusie's comparison of the cotangent-complex class with the deformation obstruction: DD.0 characterises the cotangent complex by square-zero extensions and derived derivations, and SF.4 owns infinitesimal lifting and obstruction complexes.

items.name: Splitting of the first conjugate piece and liftings modulo I²
items.statement: Let X be a p-completely flat p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The complex Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} splits in D(X), i.e. is isomorphic in D(X) to a complex with zero differentials, if and only if X admits a lifting to a p-completely flat formal scheme over A/I².
items.note: Proved here from the previous two statements; it is a property of the conjugate filtration owned by PR.2, for which the paper is a source.

items.name: Quasi-syntomic ring, morphism and cover
items.statement: A ring R is quasi-syntomic if R is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and the cotangent complex L_{R/Z_p} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1,0] (i.e. M = L_{R/Z_p} ⊗^L_R R/p satisfies M ⊗^L_R N ∈ D^{[−1,0]}(R/p) for every R/p-module N). The category of quasi-syntomic rings is QSyn. A map R → R′ of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion is a quasi-syntomic morphism (resp. a quasi-syntomic cover) if R′ is p-completely flat (resp. p-completely faithfully flat) over R and L_{R′/R} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1,0].
items.note: DD.0 defines quasisyntomic maps by p-complete flatness, bounded p-power torsion and the required mod-p cotangent amplitude and proves the compatibility with the alternative formulations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §4; DD.5 constructs the resulting site. Mathlib has the cotangent complex of an extension (Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex) but no p-complete Tor-amplitude.

items.name: Examples of quasi-syntomic rings
items.statement: (1) Any p-complete l.c.i. Noetherian ring is in QSyn. (2) Any integral perfectoid ring R — p-complete, with π^p = pu for some π ∈ R and u ∈ R^×, with Frobenius surjective on R/p and ker(θ) principal — is in QSyn; indeed L_{R/A_inf(R)} = ker(θ)/ker(θ)²[1] = R[1] and A_inf(R) is relatively perfect over Z_p modulo p, and R[p^∞] = R[p]. (3) Hence the p-completion of a smooth algebra over a perfectoid ring is quasi-syntomic, as is any p-complete bounded p^∞-torsion quotient of an integral perfectoid ring by a finite regular sequence; O_{C_p}⟨T⟩, O_{C_p}/p and F_p[T^{1/p^∞}]/(T−1) are quasi-syntomic.
items.note: DD.0 proves the lci amplitude criterion and DD.5 supplies the quasisyntomic site with its examples; Q0's integral-algebra prefix owns integral perfectoid rings with their θ and A_inf descriptions.

items.name: Quasi-syntomic site; big and small
items.statement: QSyn_qsyn^op is the site whose underlying category is the opposite of QSyn, with the Grothendieck topology generated by quasi-syntomic covers. For R ∈ QSyn, (R)_QSYN (resp. (R)_qsyn) is the big (resp. small) quasi-syntomic site of R, whose objects are all p-complete R-algebras with bounded p^∞-torsion (resp. all quasi-syntomic R-algebras, i.e. those p-complete bounded p^∞-torsion R-algebras S for which R → S is quasi-syntomic), with the quasi-syntomic topology.
items.note: DD.5 constructs the quasisyntomic site using DD.0's morphism condition. The distinction between the big and the small site is used throughout this paper, since M_Δ(G) is a sheaf on the small site while u is defined towards the big one.

items.name: Quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: A ring R is quasi-regular semiperfectoid if R ∈ QSyn and there exists a perfectoid ring S mapping surjectively onto R.
items.note: DD.5 constructs the semiperfectoid covers of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §4 and PR.2 proves the discrete prism calculation for quasi-regular semiperfectoid inputs.

items.name: Examples of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings
items.statement: Any perfectoid ring, and any p-complete bounded p^∞-torsion quotient of a perfectoid ring by a finite regular sequence, is quasi-regular semiperfectoid.
items.note: The acceptance examples named by PR.2 (regular semiperfectoid quotient, singular quasi-regular semiperfectoid algebra) and by DD.5.

items.name: Quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings form a basis
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. There exists a quasi-syntomic cover R → R′ with R′ quasi-regular semiperfectoid, and all terms of the Čech nerve R′^• are quasi-regular semiperfectoid.
items.note: DD.5 proves existence and refinement of the semiperfectoid covers used by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze; this is the statement that makes quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings a basis of the quasi-syntomic topology, and it is the engine of every descent argument in this paper.

items.name: Lifting a quasi-syntomic cover to a prism
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a quasi-syntomic A/I-algebra. There exists a prism (B, IB) ∈ (R/A)_Δ such that R → B/IB is p-completely faithfully flat. In particular, if A/I → R is a quasi-syntomic cover then (A, I) → (B, IB) is a faithfully flat map of prisms.
items.note: Q3 proves exactly this lifting theorem for quasisyntomic covers to bounded prisms, Bhatt–Scholze 7.11, together with preservation of faithful flatness under completed perfection.

items.name: André's lemma
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. Then there exists a p-completely faithfully flat map R → S of perfectoid rings such that S is absolutely integrally closed, i.e. every monic polynomial with coefficients in S has a solution.
items.note: Q3 proves Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 7.14, constructing the extension by adjoining roots of monic polynomials, lifting to a prism, perfecting and iterating transfinitely.

items.name: The morphism of topoi from the prismatic to the quasi-syntomic topos
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring. The functor u : (R)_Δ → (R)_QSYN sending (A, I) to the object R → A/I is cocontinuous, and therefore defines a morphism of topoi u : Shv((R)_Δ) → Shv((R)_QSYN).
items.note: The bridge on which the whole paper rests: it lets a p-divisible group, a sheaf on the quasi-syntomic site, be pulled back to the prismatic site. PR.5 compares the absolute prismatic site with the relative ones but plans no comparison with the quasi-syntomic site, and nothing else in the atlas plans u.

items.name: Exactness of the pullback along u
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and let 0 → G_1 → G_2 → G_3 → 0 be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on (R)_QSYN. Then 0 → u^{-1}(G_1) → u^{-1}(G_2) → u^{-1}(G_3) → 0 is exact on (R)_Δ. This applies in particular when G_1, G_2, G_3 are finite locally free group schemes over R.
items.note: Exactness of u^{-1} is what allows Ext-groups computed on the prismatic site to be compared with Ext-groups on the quasi-syntomic site; it is proved here from the lifting theorem of Q3 and belongs to the same new package as the morphism of topoi itself.

items.name: All prisms agree for a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism and R quasi-regular semiperfectoid with a surjection A/I ↠ R. Then the canonical morphisms induce isomorphisms Δ_{R/A} ≅ Δ_{R/A}^init ≅ Δ_{R/A}^{init,unbdd} of δ-rings; in particular (Δ_R, I) is the initial object of the prismatic site of R.
items.note: PR.2 proves the discrete δ/prism calculation for quasi-regular semiperfectoid inputs and the initial-prism comparison, including the regular-quotient and idempotent-retract arguments of Bhatt–Scholze §§7.7–7.10.

items.name: The prism of a quasi-regular semiperfect ring is A_crys
items.statement: Let (A, I) and R be as above and assume pR = 0. Then there is a canonical φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ_{R/A} ≅ A_crys(R).
items.note: PR.2 proves the quasi-regular semiperfect calculation in the Bhatt–Scholze §7 range; CR.0 exports the p-completed PD envelope A_crys by its universal property, so that no second A_crys is built.

items.name: The comparison with A_crys is Frobenius-twisted over W(R^♭)
items.statement: Both Δ_{R/A} and A_crys(R) are naturally W(R^♭)-algebras, but the isomorphism above restricts to the Frobenius on W(R^♭). Concretely, if R = R^♭/x for a non-zero divisor x ∈ R^♭, then Δ_{R/W(R^♭)} ≅ W(R^♭){x/p}^∧ and A_crys(R) ≅ W(R^♭){x^p/p}^∧ ≅ Δ_{R/W(R^♭)} ⊗_{W(R^♭),φ} W(R^♭).
items.note: PR.1 and PR.3 both insist that the crystalline and de Rham comparisons carry a φ_A-twisted scalar extension and that it is not an untwisted identification; PR.2 owns the semiperfect calculation in which the twist appears.

items.name: Graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring. Then N^{≥i}(Δ_R)/N^{≥i+1}(Δ_R) ≅ Fil_i^conj(Δ̄_R){i} for i ≥ 0. In particular Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R.
items.note: PR.3 proves the associated-graded description of the Nygaard filtration and its comparison with the Hodge–Tate and de Rham filtrations. The special case Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R is used constantly in this paper, since it is what makes the structure sheaf of the quasi-syntomic site a quotient of O^pris.

items.name: Künneth formula in prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. The functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A} from derived p-complete simplicial rings over A/I to derived (p,I)-complete E_∞-algebras over A preserves tensor products: for all morphisms R_1 ← R_3 → R_2 the canonical morphism Δ_{R_1/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{R_3/A}} Δ_{R_2/A} → Δ_{R_1 ⊗̂^L_{R_3} R_2/A} is an equivalence.
items.note: A general property of derived prismatic cohomology, proved here and used to compute the prismatic cohomology of a product of an abelian scheme with itself; PR.2 owns the derived functor and its base-change formulas, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Künneth formula for smooth proper formal schemes
items.statement: If X and Y are quasi-compact quasi-separated p-completely smooth p-adic formal schemes over Spf(A/I), then RΓ(X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y, Δ_{X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y/A}) ≅ RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) ⊗̂^L_A RΓ(Y, Δ_{Y/A}).
items.note: The geometric form of the Künneth formula, in the same layer as the previous item.

items.name: The sheaves O^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris and I^pris
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and let v : Shv((R)_Δ) → Shv((R)_qsyn) be the morphism of topoi induced by u. Define O^pris := v_*O_Δ, N^{≥1}O^pris := v_*N^{≥1}O_Δ and I^pris := v_*I_Δ, where I_Δ ⊆ O_Δ is the canonical invertible ideal sheaf sending a prism (B, J) ∈ (R)_Δ to J. The sheaf O^pris carries a Frobenius lift φ.
items.note: These are the coefficient sheaves of the whole theory: the pushforward to the quasi-syntomic site of the prismatic structure sheaf, of the first Nygaard piece and of the prism ideal. Nothing in the atlas plans them, because nothing plans the morphism of topoi v.

items.name: The quotient of O^pris by its first Nygaard piece
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The quotient sheaf O^pris/N^{≥1}O^pris is isomorphic to the structure sheaf O of (R)_qsyn.
items.note: The sheafified form of Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R; it is what makes the filtration quotient of an admissible object a finite locally free module over the base.

items.name: Prismatic crystal
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring. A prismatic crystal over R is an O_Δ-module M on the prismatic site (R)_Δ such that for all morphisms (B, J) → (B′, J′) in (R)_Δ the canonical morphism M(B,J) ⊗_B B′ → M(B′,J′) is an isomorphism.
items.note: PR.5 proves the equivalence with the prismatic crystals of Bhatt–Lurie on the Cartier–Witt stack, and PR.7 constructs vector-bundle crystals on the absolute site.

items.name: Finite locally free prismatic sheaves and their pushforward
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The functors v_* and v^*(−) := O_Δ ⊗_{v^♮O^pris} v^♮(−) induce mutually inverse equivalences between the category of finite locally free O_Δ-modules and the category of finite locally free O^pris-modules.
items.note: This is the theorem that justifies calling the modules on the quasi-syntomic site 'crystals': it identifies them with genuine crystals on the prismatic site. It depends on v, which nothing in the atlas plans.

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné crystal; admissibility
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. A prismatic Dieudonné crystal over R is a finite locally free O^pris-module M together with a φ-linear morphism φ_M : M → M whose linearization φ^*M → M has cokernel killed by I^pris. It is admissible if the image of the composition M →^{φ_M} M → M/I^pris·M is a finite locally free O-module F_M such that the map (O^pris/I^pris) ⊗_O F_M → M/I^pris M induced by φ_M is a monomorphism.
items.note: The central definition of the paper. Nothing in the atlas plans it: PR.7 plans prismatic F-crystals, where φ^*E[1/I] ≅ E[1/I] is an isomorphism after inverting I, but neither the minuscule condition here nor admissibility.

items.name: Injectivity of the linearized Frobenius
items.statement: For a prismatic Dieudonné crystal (M, φ_M) the linearization φ^*M → M is an isomorphism after inverting a local generator ξ̃ of I^pris, and in particular is injective, since φ^*M is ξ̃-torsion free. The same holds for a prismatic Dieudonné module (M, φ_M) over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring, with ξ̃ a generator of I.
items.note: Stated for crystals in Remark 4.6 and for modules in Remark 4.11 of the published version (arXiv Remarks 4.1.6 and 4.1.11); it is the observation that a prismatic Dieudonné crystal is in particular a prismatic F-crystal in the sense of PR.7, and it is used in every argument that inverts I.

items.name: Admissibility is the vanishing of the snake term
items.statement: Let (M, φ_M) be a prismatic Dieudonné crystal and write Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(I^pris·M) and F_M = M/Fil M. The snake lemma applied to the two rows 0 → φ^*Fil M → I^pris·M → Q → 0 and 0 → φ^*M → M → K → 0 gives an exact sequence 0 → Q → φ^*M/φ^*Fil M ≅ (O^pris/I^pris) ⊗_O F_M →^β M/I^pris M → K → 0, because I^pris·K = 0. Hence the injectivity of β required by admissibility is equivalent to Q = 0.
items.note: The working reformulation of admissibility used throughout Sections 4 and 5.

items.name: The categories DM(R) and DM^adm(R) of crystals
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. DM(R) denotes the category of prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R, with O^pris-linear morphisms commuting with Frobenius, and DM^adm(R) its full subcategory of admissible objects.
items.note: The target category of the main theorem.

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné crystals form a stack
items.statement: The fibered category of prismatic Dieudonné crystals, and the fibered category of admissible ones, over the category QSyn of quasi-syntomic rings with the quasi-syntomic topology, is a stack.
items.note: This is what reduces the main theorem to quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings; it rests on quasi-syntomic descent for finite locally free modules, which DD.5 and PR.2 plan for the underlying complexes but not for these objects.

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné module over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring; admissibility
items.statement: Let R be quasi-regular semiperfectoid with initial prism (Δ_R, I). A prismatic Dieudonné module over R is a finite locally free Δ_R-module M with a φ-linear morphism φ_M : M → M whose linearization φ^*M → M has cokernel killed by I. It is admissible if the image of M →^{φ_M} M → M/I·M is a finite locally free R ≅ Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R-module F_M such that the induced map (Δ_R/IΔ_R) ⊗_R F_M → M/IM is a monomorphism.
items.note: The concrete, module-theoretic form of the previous definition.

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné modules over a perfectoid ring are admissible
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. Then every prismatic Dieudonné module over R is admissible.
items.note: Over a perfectoid ring the Nygaard filtration on Δ_R = A_inf(R) is trivial in the relevant degree, so admissibility is automatic; this is why the perfectoid case of the classification is the input rather than a special case of the output.

items.name: Crystals and modules agree over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring. The evaluation functor (M, φ_M) ↦ (v^*M(Δ_R, I), v^*φ_M(Δ_R, I)) on the initial prism induces an equivalence between the category of (usual or admissible) prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R and the category of (usual or admissible) prismatic Dieudonné modules over R, with quasi-inverse (M, φ_M) ↦ (M ⊗_{Δ_R} O^pris, φ_M ⊗ φ_{O^pris}).
items.note: The bridge between the sheaf-theoretic and the module-theoretic descriptions; it is what turns the stack property into a reduction to quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings.

items.name: Base change of the Frobenius preimage
items.statement: Let R → R′ be a quasi-syntomic morphism of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings, let (M, φ_M) be a prismatic Dieudonné module over R and let (M′, φ_{M′}) = (M ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_{R′}, φ_M ⊗ φ_{Δ_{R′}}) be its base change. Then φ_{M′}^{-1}(IΔ_{R′}·M′) = N^{≥1}Δ_{R′}·M′ + Im(φ_M^{-1}(I·M) ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_{R′} → M′).
items.note: The formula that makes the filtration Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(I·M) compatible with base change, hence descend; it is used to prove that admissibility is a quasi-syntomic-local condition.

items.name: The categories DM(R) and DM^adm(R) of modules
items.statement: For a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring R, DM(R) also denotes the category of prismatic Dieudonné modules over R, with morphisms commuting with the Frobenius, and DM^adm(R) its full subcategory of admissible objects. The notation is deliberately the same as for crystals, because the two categories are identified by the evaluation equivalence.
items.note: The overloading of DM(R) is a deliberate convention of the paper; it must be recorded, because several statements — in particular the essential-surjectivity theorem — are about modules while their wording says 'crystals'.

items.name: Frame and u-morphism of frames
items.statement: A frame A = (A, Fil A, φ, φ_1) consists of classically (p,d)-adically complete rings A and R = A/Fil A, for some d ∈ A and some ideal Fil A, a lift of Frobenius φ and a φ-linear map φ_1 : Fil A → A, called the divided Frobenius, such that φ = ϖ φ_1 on Fil A, with ϖ = φ(d). Given frames A, A′ and a unit u ∈ A′, a u-morphism of frames α : A → A′ is a ring morphism α : A → A′ intertwining φ and φ′, carrying Fil A into Fil A′, and satisfying φ_1′ ∘ α = u α ∘ φ_1 and α(ϖ) = u ϖ′.
items.note: Frames and windows in the sense of Lau and Zink are the technical language in which admissibility is handled; the atlas plans no frames, no windows and no displays.

items.name: The two frames attached to an oriented prism
items.statement: Let (A, I = (d)) be an oriented prism. The frame A_d = (A, (d), φ, φ_1) has φ_1 defined by φ_1(dx) = φ(x), using that A is d-torsion free; here φ = φ(d)φ_1 on Fil A = (d). When d = φ(d′) for some d′ ∈ A, the Nygaard frame A_Nyg = (A, N^{≥1}A, φ, φ_1) has φ_1 = φ/d on N^{≥1}A; here φ = d φ_1 on Fil A. In the first case the divided Frobenius is with respect to φ(d), in the second with respect to d.
items.note: These are the two frames through which the paper reads its objects: windows over A_d are minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules, windows over A_Nyg are admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules.

items.name: Window over a frame
items.statement: A window M = (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) over a frame A consists of a finite locally free A-module M, an A-submodule Fil M ⊆ M and φ-linear maps φ_M : M → M and φ_{M,1} : Fil M → M such that: Fil A·M ⊆ Fil M and M/Fil M is a finite locally free R-module; φ_{M,1}(am) = φ_1(a)φ_M(m) for a ∈ Fil A and m ∈ M; φ_M(m) = ϖ φ_{M,1}(m) for m ∈ Fil M; and φ_{M,1}(Fil M) + φ_M(M) generates M as an A-module. Morphisms are A-linear maps preserving the filtrations and commuting with φ_M and φ_{M,1}; the category is Win(A).
items.note: The category through which admissibility is characterised.

items.name: α-morphisms of windows and base change
items.statement: If α : A → A′ is a u-morphism of frames, an α-morphism of windows f : M → M′ is an A-linear map f : M → M′ intertwining φ_M and φ_{M′}, sending Fil M into Fil M′ and satisfying φ_{M′,1} ∘ f = u f ∘ φ_{M,1}. There is a base-change functor α^* : Win(A) → Win(A′) characterised by the universal property that morphisms α^*M → M′ in Win(A′) are the α-morphisms M → M′; concretely M′ = A′ ⊗_A M, Fil M′ is generated by Fil A′·M′ and the image of Fil M, and φ_{M′}, φ_{M′,1} are determined by the requirement that m ↦ 1 ⊗ m be an α-morphism.
items.note: The base-change formalism for windows; it is what transports the prismatic Dieudonné functor along the frame morphism Δ_{R,Nyg} → W(R) in the comparison with displays.

items.name: Normal decompositions of windows
items.statement: Let A = (A, Fil A, φ, φ_1) be a frame such that every finite projective A/Fil A-module lifts to a finite projective A-module, and let (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) be a window over A. Then there exist finite projective A-modules L, T with M = L ⊕ T and Fil M = L ⊕ Fil A·T. Moreover, given L and T, there is a bijection between φ-semilinear isomorphisms Ψ : L ⊕ T → L ⊕ T (φ-semilinear maps that become isomorphisms after linearization) and A-window structures on the pair (L ⊕ T, L ⊕ Fil A·T).
items.note: Lau's normal decomposition, in the generality needed here; it is the computational device behind the comparison of windows with Breuil–Kisin modules.

items.name: The filtration of a window is the Frobenius preimage
items.statement: Let A be a frame as above with ϖ a non-zero divisor and Fil A = φ^{-1}(ϖ A). Then for every window (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) over A one has Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(ϖ M) (the inclusion ⊆ always holds). Moreover φ_M : M → M induces an injection M/Fil M → M/ϖM, which extends to an injection A/ϖ ⊗_{A/Fil A} M/Fil M → M/I of a locally direct summand.
items.note: This is the statement that identifies the window structure with the admissibility condition: the filtration is determined by the Frobenius, and the extra injectivity is exactly admissibility.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin module; minuscule
items.statement: Let (A, I = (d)) be a prism. A Breuil–Kisin module (M, φ_M) over (A, I) is a finite free A-module M together with an isomorphism φ_M : φ^*M[1/I] ≅ M[1/I]. If φ_M(φ^*M) ⊆ M with cokernel killed by I, then (M, φ_M) is called minuscule. BK(A) denotes the category of Breuil–Kisin modules over A and BK_min(A) ⊆ BK(A) its full subcategory of minuscule objects.
items.note: PR.7 constructs prismatic F-crystals — vector bundles E with φ^*E[1/I] ≅ E[1/I] — and compares their evaluation on the Breuil–Kisin prism with R07's Kisin functor; R07.4 constructs the power-series coefficient ring, Frobenius modules and the height bound. The minuscule condition is the height-one case they plan. The same definition is printed a second time in the published Definition 5.11 (arXiv Definition 5.2.4), which is recorded below as a source issue.

items.name: The cokernel of a minuscule Breuil–Kisin module is projective
items.statement: If (M, φ_M) is a minuscule Breuil–Kisin module over (A, I), the cokernel N of φ_M(φ^*M) ⊆ M is a finite projective A/I-module. Indeed N is pseudocoherent as an A-module, hence as an A/I-module; for k the residue field of Spec(A/I) at a closed point, k̄ ⊗^L_{A/I} N = W(k̄) ⊗^L_A N is a perfect complex of W(k̄)-modules, hence bounded, so N has a finite resolution by finite projective A/I-modules; since N has projective dimension ≤ 1 over A it is projective over A/I.
items.note: An argument supplied by the referee; it is what makes the minuscule condition equivalent to the locally-free-cokernel condition used elsewhere.

items.name: Windows over the d-frame are minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Let (A, (d)) be an oriented prism. The functor (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) ↦ (Fil M, d·φ_{M,1}) induces an equivalence between the category of windows over the frame A_d and the category BK_min(A) of minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules.
items.note: Cais–Lau's equivalence, in the prismatic formulation; it is the first half of the comparison with the Breuil–Kisin classification in Section 5.2. Nothing in the atlas plans windows.

items.name: Finite projective modules over a henselian pair
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a henselian pair. The base change M ↦ M ⊗_A A/I induces a bijection on isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over A and over A/I.
items.note: A standard fact about henselian pairs (Clausen–Mathew–Morrow). Mathlib has HenselianRing and HenselianLocalRing but no statement about projective modules over a henselian pair, and the atlas's henselian layer, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:henselian, plans approximation for adic spaces rather than this; the Part II needs it in its preliminaries, and a reviewer who prefers a more foundational owner may move it there.

items.name: The prism of a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring is henselian along ker θ
items.statement: For R quasi-regular semiperfectoid, the pair (Δ_R, ker(θ)) is henselian.
items.note: Used together with the previous item to lift finite projective modules from R to Δ_R, in the proof of essential surjectivity.

items.name: Windows over the Nygaard frame are admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring. Fix a generator ξ̃ = φ(ξ) of the ideal I of the prism (Δ_R, I), giving the frame Δ_{R,Nyg} with d = ξ̃. The forgetful functor Win(Δ_{R,Nyg}) → DM(R), (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) ↦ (M, φ_M), is fully faithful with essential image the subcategory DM^adm(R).
items.note: The theorem that makes admissibility usable: an admissible prismatic Dieudonné module is the same thing as a window over the Nygaard frame, so the window machinery applies to it.

items.name: Equivalence of unit Frobenius modules along a nilpotent surjection
items.statement: Let A → B be a surjection of bounded prisms with kernel J ⊆ A. Assume that the Frobenius φ of A is topologically nilpotent on J for the (p,I)-adic topology, and that (A, J) is henselian. Then the base-change functor φ-Mod_A^unit → φ-Mod_B^unit, (M, φ_M) ↦ (M ⊗_A B, φ_M ⊗_A B), is an equivalence.
items.note: The Frobenius-nilpotence deformation argument; together with the next item it gives essential surjectivity along the surjections used in Section 4.9.

items.name: Equivalence of window categories along a nilpotent surjection
items.statement: Let (A, (ξ̃)) → (B, (ξ̃)) be a surjection of oriented bounded prisms with kernel J contained in N^{≥1}A, with ξ̃ = φ(ξ) for some ξ ∈ A and (A, ξ̃) bounded. Assume that φ_1 is pointwise topologically nilpotent on J and that (A, J) is henselian. Then the base-change functor induces an equivalence Win(A_Nyg) ≃ Win((B, N^{≥1}A/J, A/N^{≥1}A, φ, φ_1)).
items.note: The window form of the previous statement; it is the engine of the essential-surjectivity argument.

items.name: Faithfulness of base change for prismatic Dieudonné modules
items.statement: Let R → R′ be a morphism of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings such that J = ker(Δ_R → Δ_{R′}) is contained in N^{≥1}Δ_R, is stable by φ_1, and φ_1 is topologically nilpotent on J (for some, equivalently any, choice of generator of I). Then the base-change functors DM(R) → DM(R′) and DM^adm(R) → DM^adm(R′) are faithful.
items.note: The faithfulness half of the descent argument.

items.name: Faithfulness of base change for windows
items.statement: More generally, if A → A′ is a 1-morphism of frames whose kernel J is contained in Fil A, is stable by φ_1 and on which φ_1 is topologically nilpotent, then the base-change functor Win(A) → Win(A′) is faithful.
items.note: The general frame-theoretic form of the previous item, used again in Section 5.2 for the Breuil–Kisin prism.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring and G a p-divisible group over R. Define M_Δ(G) := Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris), the sheaf Ext of abelian sheaves on the small quasi-syntomic site, and φ_{M_Δ(G)} as the endomorphism induced by φ on O^pris. The pair (M_Δ(G), φ_{M_Δ(G)}) is the prismatic Dieudonné crystal of G.
items.note: The construction whose properties are the content of the paper. It has no analogue in the atlas: R07.2 plans classical Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields, not an Ext-sheaf construction on a quasi-syntomic site.

items.name: There are no homomorphisms from a p-divisible group to a p-complete sheaf
items.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over a p-complete ring R. Then Hom(G, Q) = 0 for every derived p-adically complete quasi-syntomic sheaf Q: the finite locally free group schemes G[p^n] are syntomic over R, so multiplication by p on G is surjective in the syntomic topology, and hence the derived p-completion of G on the big quasi-syntomic site is T_pG placed in degree −1; there are no morphisms from D^{≤−1} to D^{≥0}. In particular Hom(G, O^pris) = 0 and Hom(G, N^{≥1}O^pris) = 0.
items.note: The vanishing that makes Ext^1 the right invariant, and that is used repeatedly to identify Ext^1(G, −) with Hom(T_pG, −).

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal as a pushforward
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism M_Δ(G) ≅ v_*(Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(G), O_Δ)).
items.note: The first step in transporting the construction to the prismatic site, where crystallinity can be proved.

items.name: Exactness of the universal cover sequence
items.statement: Define the universal cover G̃ := lim_{×p} G of G. Then the sequences 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0 of sheaves on (R)_qsyn and 0 → u^{-1}T_pG → u^{-1}G̃ → u^{-1}G → 0 of sheaves on (R)_Δ are exact for the quasi-syntomic topology.
items.note: The device that replaces G by its Tate module.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal as a Hom from the Tate module
items.statement: There are canonical isomorphisms M_Δ(G) ≅ Hom_{(R)_qsyn}(T_pG, O^pris) ≅ v_*Hom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(T_pG), O_Δ).
items.note: The description that turns the Ext-sheaf into a Hom-sheaf; it is the form used in the proof of full faithfulness.

items.name: Universal vector extension and the Hodge–Tate map
items.statement: The universal vector extension E(G) of G is an extension of sheaves on (R)_qsyn, 0 → ω_{Ǧ} → E(G) → G → 0, defined as in Messing (this makes sense since R is p-complete), or equivalently as the pushout of the universal cover sequence 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0 along the Hodge–Tate map HT : T_pG → ω_{Ǧ}, which sends f ∈ T_pG = Hom_R(Q_p/Z_p, G), viewed by Cartier duality as an element of Hom_R(Ǧ, μ_{p^∞}), to f^*dT/T, where dT/T is the canonical generator of ω_{μ_{p^∞}}.
items.note: Messing's universal vector extension, in the quasi-syntomic sheaf-theoretic form used here. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 plans p-divisible groups, their Tate modules and Cartier duality, and R07.6 Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory, but the universal vector extension itself is not named by any layer; it is used here only to interpret the construction, so it is routed with the rest.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné module of a p-divisible group
items.statement: Let R be quasi-regular semiperfectoid and let G be a p-divisible group over R. Define M_Δ(G) := Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris) ≅ Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(G), O_Δ) and φ_{M_Δ(G)} as the endomorphism induced by φ on O^pris. The pair (M_Δ(G), φ_{M_Δ(G)}) is the prismatic Dieudonné module of G.
items.note: The global-sections version of the construction over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid base.

items.name: Comparison of the prismatic and crystalline structure sheaves
items.statement: Let R′ be a quasi-syntomic F_p-algebra. Then there is a canonical isomorphism O^pris(R′) → O^crys(R′) identifying N^{≥1}O^pris(R′) with J^crys(R′).
items.note: The sheaf-level form of Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R), including the identification of the Nygaard piece with the PD ideal; PR.2 and CR.0 plan the ring-level comparison, not this comparison of sheaves on the quasi-syntomic site.

items.name: Comparison with the crystalline Dieudonné functor
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring with pR = 0 and G a p-divisible group over R. Then there is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism M_Δ(G) ≅ v_*^crys(Ext^1_{(R/Z_p)_{crys,pr}}((u^crys)^{-1}(G), O^crys)) from the prismatic Dieudonné crystal of G to the pushforward of the crystalline Dieudonné crystal of G. In particular, if R is quasi-regular semiperfect, M_Δ(G) is isomorphic to the evaluation M^crys(G) on A_crys(R) of the crystalline Dieudonné crystal, compatibly with Frobenius.
items.note: The theorem that connects the new theory to Berthelot–Breen–Messing's; it is the source of the corollary on the crystalline Dieudonné functor recorded above.

items.name: Evaluation on a PD thickening
items.statement: For every p-divisible group G over R there is a natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism v^*(M_Δ(G))(D, (p)) ≅ D(G)(D), where D(G)(D) is the evaluation of the contravariant crystalline Dieudonné crystal of G on the PD thickening D → R.
items.note: The pointwise form of the crystalline comparison, used in Section 5.2 over O_K.

items.name: A minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module is determined by a triple
items.statement: A prismatic Dieudonné module (M, φ_M) over O_C, i.e. a minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module, is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by the triple (T_M, M_crys, α_M), where T_M = M[1/ξ̃]^{φ_M=1} is a finite free Z_p-module, M_crys = M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys is a φ-module over A_crys, and α_M : T_M ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ M_crys ⊗_{A_crys} B_crys is the φ-equivariant isomorphism coming from M[1/ξ̃]^{φ_M=1} → M[1/ξ̃].
items.note: A structural description of minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over O_C in crystalline terms. AInfCohomology AI.2 owns Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and proves Fargues' classification by pairs (T, Ξ) with Ξ a B_dR^+-lattice; this crystalline triple is the companion description, so the paper is a source for AI.2.

items.name: Comparison with the Scholze–Weinstein functor
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. The functor G ↦ M_Δ(G) from BT(R) to DM(R) coincides with the naive dual (−)^* = Hom_{A_inf(R)}(−, A_inf(R)) of the functor M^SW of Scholze–Weinstein.
items.note: The identification of the perfectoid case with the known classification, which is the input to the main theorem.

items.name: The classification over a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. The prismatic Dieudonné functor M_Δ takes values in DM^adm(R) ≅ DM(R) and induces an antiequivalence between BT(R) and DM^adm(R) ≅ DM(R).
items.note: The base case of the main theorem, deduced from Lau's and Scholze–Weinstein's results; the proof of the main theorem requires it as an input, in fact only for perfectoid valuation rings with algebraically closed and spherically complete fraction field.

items.name: Exactness of the classification over a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. The functor M_Δ is exact and has an exact quasi-inverse.
items.note: Stated in Remark 4.50 of the published version (arXiv Remark 4.3.8), with the argument given in Section 5.1 for finite locally free group schemes and noted to apply verbatim for p-divisible groups; it is used for the exact antiequivalence in Section 5.1.

items.name: Comparison with the classical Dieudonné module over a perfect field
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and let G be a p-divisible group over k. One has a canonical W(k)-linear Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism M_Δ(G) ≅ M^cl(G) with the classical (contravariant) Dieudonné module.
items.note: The identification with classical Dieudonné theory. R07.2 plans classical Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields with Frobenius, Verschiebung, heights and slopes; this comparison statement is what links the new functor to them, but it presupposes the new functor, so it is routed with it.

items.name: The sheaf Q on the prismatic site
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring with pR = 0. Define the sheaf Q on (R)_Δ by the exact sequence 0 → O_Δ → O_Δ[1/p] → Q → 0.
items.note: An auxiliary coefficient sheaf giving a Hom-description of the prismatic Dieudonné crystal in characteristic p.

items.name: Hom-description of the prismatic Dieudonné crystal in characteristic p
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring with pR = 0 and G a p-divisible group over R. The connecting map of 0 → O_Δ → O_Δ[1/p] → Q → 0 induces an isomorphism Hom_{(R)_qsyn}(G, v_*Q) = v_*Hom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, Q) ≅ M_Δ(G).
items.note: The characteristic-p analogue of the classical description by Witt covectors; the paper asks (Question 4.54 of the published version, arXiv Question 4.3.12) what the relation between v_*Q and the sheaf CW of Witt covectors is over a perfect field.

items.name: A functorial resolution of an abelian group object in a topos
items.statement: Let G be an abelian group object in a topos 𝔛. Then there exists a natural functorial resolution C(G)_• := (… → Z[X_2] → Z[X_1] → Z[X_0]) ≃ G in which each X_i ∈ 𝔛 is a finite disjoint union of products of copies of G.
items.note: A general topos-theoretic construction (in the style of Breen and of Scholze's Berkeley notes) used here to compute the Ext-sheaves of a p-divisible group. Nothing in the atlas plans it, and the paper uses it only for that computation, so it is routed with the rest; a reviewer may prefer to give a more foundational layer ownership of it.

items.name: Derived Yoneda lemma in a topos
items.statement: Let X ∈ 𝔛 be any object and F ∈ Ab(𝔛) an abelian group object. Then RΓ(X, F) ≅ RHom_{Ab(𝔛)}(Z[X], F), where Z[X] is the free abelian group on X.
items.note: The companion of the previous item; together they turn the Ext computation into a cohomology computation on products of copies of G.

items.name: Hodge and de Rham cohomology of an abelian scheme
items.statement: Let X be an abelian scheme over a base Ā. For all k ≥ 0 (resp. all i, j ≥ 0) the Ā-module H^k(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) (resp. H^i(X, Ω^j_{X/Ā})) is finite locally free and its formation commutes with base change. Moreover the algebra H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) is alternating and the canonical algebra morphism ∧^*H^1(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) → H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Berthelot–Breen–Messing 2.5.2. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 constructs relative H^1_dR with its Hodge exact sequence, base change and cup product, and says explicitly that these are degree-one statements; the finite local freeness in all degrees and the exterior-algebra structure are what this paper needs, so it is a source for that layer.

items.name: Degeneration of the conjugate spectral sequence for an abelian scheme
items.statement: For X the p-adic completion of an abelian scheme over a bounded prism (A, I), the conjugate spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^i(X, Ω^j_{X/Ā}){−j} ⇒ H^{i+j}(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) degenerates, and each term as well as the abutment commutes with base change in (A, I). Moreover H^*(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Λ^*H^1(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) is an exterior Ā-algebra on H^1(X, Δ̄_{X/A}).
items.note: The prismatic form of the previous statement, proved from the conjugate filtration of PR.2; it is the computation that makes the Ext-sheaves of an abelian scheme finite locally free.

items.name: A fibrewise isomorphism criterion
items.statement: Let S be a ring and g : M → N a morphism of S-modules with M finitely generated and N finite projective. If g ⊗_S k(x) : M ⊗_S k(x) → N ⊗_S k(x) is an isomorphism for every closed point x ∈ Spec(S), then g is an isomorphism.
items.note: An elementary commutative-algebra lemma used to check the Ext computation fibrewise; the libraries have finitely generated and finite projective modules (Module.Finite, Module.Projective) but not this criterion.

items.name: Reduced prismatic Ext-sheaves of an abelian scheme
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and f : X → Spf(R) the p-adic completion of an abelian scheme over Spec(R). Then (1) Ext^i_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(X), Ō_Δ) = 0 for i = 0, 2; (2) Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(X), Ō_Δ) is a prismatic crystal over R, it is isomorphic to R^1f_{Δ,*}(Ō_Δ) for f_Δ : Shv((X)_Δ) → Shv((R)_Δ) the induced morphism of topoi, and it is locally free of rank 2 dim(X) over Ō_Δ.
items.note: The Hodge–Tate step of the computation.

items.name: Primitive elements in an exterior algebra
items.statement: Let S be a ring and M a projective S-module. Then {x ∈ Λ(M) : μ^*(x) = 1 ⊗ x + x ⊗ 1} = Λ^1M, where μ^* : Λ(M) → Λ(M ⊕ M) ≅ Λ(M) ⊗_S Λ(M) is the comultiplication coming from the diagonal M → M ⊕ M.
items.note: The algebraic lemma that isolates H^1 inside the exterior algebra, hence identifies the Ext-sheaf with the degree-one prismatic cohomology. Mathlib has ExteriorAlgebra and its exterior powers but not this characterisation of primitives.

items.name: Prismatic Ext-sheaves of an abelian scheme
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and f : X → Spf(R) the p-adic completion of an abelian scheme over Spec(R). Then (1) Ext^i_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(X), O_Δ) = 0 for i = 0, 2; (2) Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}(X), O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal over R, isomorphic to R^1f_{Δ,*}(O_Δ), and locally free of rank 2 dim(X) over O_Δ.
items.note: The prismatic step of the computation, deduced from the Hodge-Tate one by the conjugate filtration and the exterior-algebra structure.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of an abelian scheme
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and X the p-completion of an abelian scheme over R. The O^pris-module M_Δ(X[p^∞]) = Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(X[p^∞], O^pris) is a finite locally free O^pris-module of rank 2 dim(X), given by R^1f_{Δ,*}O_Δ.
items.note: The case of the main construction that is computed directly; every other case is deduced from it by embedding a finite locally free group scheme into an abelian scheme.

items.name: Prismatic cohomology of an abelian scheme
items.statement: With the notation above, the prismatic cohomology R^*f_{Δ,*}O_Δ is a finite locally free crystal on (R)_Δ and an exterior algebra on the locally free crystal R^1f_{Δ,*}(O_Δ) of rank 2 dim(X).
items.note: A statement about prismatic cohomology rather than about Dieudonné theory, but proved here as a by-product; PR.1 and PR.2 own prismatic cohomology, and a reviewer may prefer to route it there.

items.name: Raynaud's embedding theorem
items.statement: Let S be a scheme and let G be a finite locally free group scheme over S. Then Zariski-locally on S there exist a projective abelian scheme A and a closed immersion G ↪ A of group schemes over S.
items.note: Raynaud's theorem, in the form of Berthelot–Breen–Messing 3.1.1. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 owns finite locally free group schemes, their subgroups, quotients and fpqc descent, and proves Raynaud's other theorem on generic-fibre full faithfulness, but not this embedding theorem; the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Prismatic Ext-sheaves of a finite locally free group scheme
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and G a finite locally free group scheme over R. Then Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of locally finitely presented O_Δ-modules.
items.note: The first consequence of Raynaud's embedding theorem and the abelian-scheme computation.

items.name: Recognising truncated Barsotti–Tate groups by the coLie complex
items.statement: Let G be a finite locally free group scheme killed by p^n over a scheme S with p^nO_S = 0, and let ℓ_G be its coLie complex. Set ω_G = H^0(ℓ_G), n_G = H^{-1}(ℓ_G), t_G = H^0(ℓ̌_G) and ν_G = H^1(ℓ̌_G). Grothendieck's duality formula identifies ℓ̌_G with τ^{≤1}RHom(G^*, G_a), giving a canonical morphism φ_G : ν_G → t_G. Then G is a BT_n if and only if t_G and t_{G^*} are locally free and φ_G and φ_{G^*} are isomorphisms. In that situation ω_G is finite locally free of rank the dimension dim(G) of G, and ν_{G^*} is finite locally free of rank h − dim(G), where h is the height of G.
items.note: Illusie's criterion, Corollaire 2.2.5 of Déformations de groupes de Barsotti–Tate. R07.1 owns finite locally free and p-divisible groups and their level structure; the coLie complex criterion for truncated Barsotti–Tate groups is not planned there, and the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: The prismatic crystal of a truncated Barsotti–Tate group
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring and G a truncated Barsotti–Tate group over R of level n. Then Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of finite locally free O_Δ/p^n-modules.
items.note: The truncated step towards the p-divisible case.

items.name: The prismatic crystal of a p-divisible group is finite locally free
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring and G a p-divisible group over R. Then Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of finite locally free O_Δ-modules of rank the height of G. In particular, if R is quasi-syntomic, M_Δ(G) is a finite locally free O^pris-module of rank the height of G.
items.note: The finiteness statement underlying the whole theory.

items.name: Lifting p-divisible groups along a henselian pair
items.statement: Let (C, J) be a henselian pair and let Ḡ be a p-divisible group over C/J. Then there exists a p-divisible group G over C with G ⊗_C C/J ≅ Ḡ.
items.note: A deformation statement for p-divisible groups along henselian pairs. R07.1 owns p-divisible groups and R07.2 the deformation results for them over nilpotent thickenings; the henselian-pair statement is stronger and is not planned, so the paper is a source for R07.1.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group is admissible
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring and G a p-divisible group over R. The pair (M_Δ(G), φ_{M_Δ(G)}) is an admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystal over R.
items.note: The first main theorem, stated as Theorem 1.13 in the published version (arXiv Theorem 1.4.1): the construction lands where it should.

items.name: Exactness of the prismatic Dieudonné functor
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The functor M_Δ : BT(R) → DM(R), G ↦ M_Δ(G), is exact.
items.note: Used for the classification of finite locally free group schemes in Section 5.1.

items.name: Compatibility with Cartier duality
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. For every p-divisible group G over R the map Φ_G : M_Δ(G)^∨ ⊗_{O^pris} M_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) → M_Δ(Ǧ) is an isomorphism.
items.note: The duality statement; it is the reason the computation of M_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) in Section 4.7 is needed.

items.name: The main theorem: the prismatic Dieudonné functor is an antiequivalence
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The prismatic Dieudonné functor M_Δ : BT(R) → DM^adm(R) is an antiequivalence between the category of p-divisible groups over R and the category of admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R.
items.note: The main theorem of the paper, stated as Theorem 1.16 in the published version (arXiv Theorem 1.4.4); it extends immediately to p-divisible groups over a quasi-syntomic formal scheme.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of an étale p-divisible group
items.statement: The O^pris-module M_Δ(Q_p/Z_p) is freely generated by the isomorphism class of the extension of O^pris by Q_p/Z_p obtained as the pushout of 0 → Z_p → Q_p → Q_p/Z_p → 0 on (R)_qsyn along the canonical morphism Z_p → O^pris. More generally, if G is an étale p-divisible group then M_Δ(G) ≅ Hom_{(R)_qsyn}(T_p(G), Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} O^pris.
items.note: The étale case, computed directly.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{−1}
items.statement: Let O_Δ{−1} be the sheaf O_Δ{−1} = Hom_{(Z_p)_Δ}(u^{-1}(Z_p(1)), O_Δ) on the absolute prismatic site of Z_p, with Z_p(1) := T_pμ_{p^∞}.
items.note: PR.3 constructs the Breuil–Kisin twists, by descent when I is not oriented, and PR.5 the intrinsic twists of the absolute theory.

items.name: Trivialisation of the Breuil–Kisin twist over the q-prism
items.statement: The O_Δ-linear map O_Δ → O_Δ{−1} sending 1 to ℓ_q, of sheaves on the category of all prisms over (A, I) = (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), is an isomorphism. Moreover the Frobenius on O_Δ{−1} sends ℓ_q to [p]_qℓ_q.
items.note: The explicit generator ℓ_q of the twist, built from the divided q-logarithm; it is the computation of M_Δ(μ_{p^∞}). PR.3 constructs the twists abstractly and PR.6 plans the q-crystalline charts, but this explicit trivialisation is proved here.

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of a multiplicative p-divisible group
items.statement: Let G be a multiplicative p-divisible group over R. Then there is a canonical isomorphism u^{-1}(Hom(G, μ_{p^∞})) ⊗_{Z_p} O_Δ ≅ Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ)|_{(R/A)_Δ}, induced by sending f : G → μ_{p^∞} to the evaluation on ℓ_q of the morphism Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}μ_{p^∞}, O_Δ)|_{(R/A)_Δ} → Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ)|_{(R/A)_Δ} induced by f.
items.note: The multiplicative case, dual to the étale one.

items.name: The functor on morphisms from Q_p/Z_p to μ_{p^∞}
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring over Z_p^cycl. Then the morphism Z_p(1)(R) ≅ Hom_R(Q_p/Z_p, μ_{p^∞}) →^{M_Δ(−)} Hom_{DM(R)}(M_Δ(μ_{p^∞}), M_Δ(Q_p/Z_p)) ≅ Δ_R^{φ=ξ̃} is given by the map sending x ∈ Z_p(1)(R) to log_q([x^{1/p}]_{θ̃}) ∈ Δ_R^{φ=ξ̃}.
items.note: The explicit computation of the functor on the basic morphisms; together with Bhatt–Lurie's Theorem 7.5.6 it already gives full faithfulness in that special case.

items.name: Full faithfulness over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: If R is a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring, the prismatic Dieudonné functor over R is fully faithful for p-divisible groups.
items.note: The first half of the main theorem.

items.name: The Tate module as a Frobenius kernel
items.statement: If G is a p-divisible group over R, there is a natural (in R and G) identification of quasi-syntomic sheaves T_pǦ ≅ ker(N^{≥1}M_Δ(G) →^{φ/ξ̃ − 1} M_Δ(G)).
items.note: The recovery of the Tate module from the prismatic Dieudonné crystal, obtained from Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze's and Bhatt–Lurie's computation of the Frobenius fixed points of the Nygaard piece; it is the key to full faithfulness.

items.name: Full faithfulness of the right adjoint on Tate modules
items.statement: The functor R is fully faithful on the subcategory of Sh_R^op spanned by the Tate modules of p-divisible groups over R.
items.note: The formal step that turns the previous identification into full faithfulness.

items.name: The strengthened Frobenius-fixed-point sequence
items.statement: Bhatt–Lurie's Theorem 7.5.6 gives a short exact sequence 0 → T_pG_m → N^{≥1}O^pris →^{φ/ξ̃ − 1} O^pris → 0. Applying RHom_{(R)_qsyn}(T_pG, −) and using Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(T_pG, T_pG_m) = Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(G, μ_{p^∞}) = 0 gives a short exact sequence 0 → T_pǦ → N^{≥1}M_Δ(Ǧ) →^{φ/ξ̃ − 1} M_Δ(Ǧ) → 0 and hence RΓ((R)_qsyn, T_pǦ) ≅ fib(N^{≥1}M_Δ(Ǧ) →^{φ/ξ̃ − 1} M_Δ(Ǧ)).
items.note: The strengthening pointed out by Akhil Mathew and the referee: not only the kernel but the whole complex is computed, so the cohomology of the Tate module is recovered from the prismatic Dieudonné crystal.

items.name: Essential surjectivity along a special surjection
items.statement: For the surjection of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings considered in the proof, the base-change functor DM^adm(S) → DM^adm(R) on admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules is essentially surjective.
items.note: The first step of the essential-surjectivity argument.

items.name: Essential surjectivity from a perfectoid ring
items.statement: With the notation of the proof, the natural functor DM^adm(S̃) → DM^adm(S) is essentially surjective.
items.note: The step that reduces to the perfectoid case, where the classification is known.

items.name: Topological nilpotence of the divided Frobenius on the kernel
items.statement: With the notation from the proof of the preceding lemma, φ(ker(α)) ⊆ ξ̃Δ_S and φ_1 := φ/ξ̃ is topologically nilpotent on ker(α).
items.note: The hypothesis needed to apply the window equivalence along a nilpotent surjection. It is the same kind of statement as the one whose proof the 2025 erratum retracts in Section 5.3, but for a different map and with a different proof; the erratum states explicitly that the faulty argument is not used anywhere else in the paper.

items.name: Presentation of a prismatic envelope for a rank-one element
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, let d ∈ A be distinguished and let x ∈ A be of rank 1. Then for n ≥ 0 there exist natural (in A and x) elements z_n ∈ A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} such that φ^n(d)φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}·z_n = x^{p^n}. Moreover, for all n ≥ 0, δ^n(x/d) lies in the subring A[z_0, …, z_n] of A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} generated by z_0, …, z_n.
items.note: An explicit presentation of a prismatic envelope. PR.0 constructs prismatic envelopes by δ-adjunction and derived completion and proves their universal properties and flatness; this concrete description is proved here, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Essential surjectivity over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring. Then the prismatic Dieudonné functor M_Δ(−) : BT(R) → DM^adm(R), from the category of p-divisible groups over R to the category of admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules over R, is essentially surjective.
items.note: The second half of the main theorem. Both the arXiv version and the published version write 'crystals' where the displayed functor and the proof both mean 'modules'; this is recorded below as a source issue, and the statement above uses the corrected wording.

items.name: An explicit quasi-inverse
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The functor G from DM^adm(R) to abelian sheaves on (R)_qsyn sending M to (M^∨)^{φ=1} ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p/Z_p, where M^∨ is the O^pris-linear dual, is a quasi-inverse of the prismatic Dieudonné functor. It seems difficult to prove directly that G takes values in p-divisible groups. For étale p-divisible groups the main theorem gives an equivalence between Z_p-local systems on R and finite locally free O^pris-modules (resp. Δ_R-modules when R is quasi-regular semiperfectoid) M with an isomorphism φ_M : φ^*M ≅ M, generalising Katz's correspondence over a perfect field.
items.note: The explicit quasi-inverse, and the étale specialisation of the main theorem.

items.name: Torsion prismatic Dieudonné module
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. A torsion prismatic Dieudonné module over R is a triple (M, φ_M, ψ_M) where M is a finitely presented A_inf(R)-module of projective dimension ≤ 1 annihilated by a power of p, and φ_M : M → M and ψ_M : M → M are respectively φ-linear and φ^{-1}-linear and satisfy φ_M ∘ ψ_M = ξ̃ and ψ_M ∘ φ_M = ξ. The category of these is DM_tors(R); it is an exact category.
items.note: The torsion analogue of a prismatic Dieudonné module. AInfCohomology AI.2 builds finitely presented A_inf-modules with torsion decompositions and warns that the category is not abelian; the pair (φ_M, ψ_M) with these two relations is the extra structure introduced here.

items.name: Base change of torsion prismatic Dieudonné modules is exact
items.statement: Let R → R′ be a morphism of perfectoid rings and M ∈ DM_tors(R). Then M ⊗_{A_inf(R)} A_inf(R′) is concentrated in degree 0. In particular the base-change functor DM_tors(R) → DM_tors(R′) is exact.
items.note: The exactness needed to descend the classification.

items.name: The categories B_S and C_S
items.statement: If S is a p-complete ring, B_S (resp. C_S) denotes the category whose objects are O_Δ-modules on (S)_Δ (resp. O_Δ-modules on (S)_Δ endowed with a φ-linear Frobenius), and whose morphisms are the O_Δ-linear morphisms (resp. the O_Δ-linear morphisms commuting with Frobenius).
items.note: Bookkeeping categories for the proof of the classification of finite locally free group schemes.

items.name: Classification of finite locally free group schemes over a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. There is a natural exact antiequivalence H ↦ (M_Δ(H), φ_{M_Δ(H)}, ψ_{M_Δ(H)}) between the exact category of finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over R and the exact category DM_tors(R) of torsion prismatic Dieudonné modules over R, such that the A_inf(R)-module M_Δ(H) is given by M_Δ(H) = Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ) and φ_{M_Δ(H)} is induced by the Frobenius of O_Δ. Exactness includes the non-formal assertion that the inverse equivalence is exact.
items.note: A similar statement is in Lau's work; the differences are that p ≥ 3 is not assumed and that the underlying A_inf-module is given by an explicit formula. It is the result used by Česnavičius–Scholze on purity for flat cohomology.

items.name: Torsion-freeness of the prismatic cohomology of a syntomic algebra
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion free, and let S be a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra (i.e. S/p ≅ S ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p and (A/I)/p → S/p is syntomic). Then H^0(S, Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion free.
items.note: A general statement about prismatic cohomology proved here; PR.1 and PR.2 own prismatic cohomology and its torsion behaviour, so the paper is a source for those layers.

items.name: Cartier duality for finite locally free group schemes
items.statement: Let H be a finite locally free group scheme of p-power order over a quasi-syntomic ring R. There is a natural isomorphism τ_{≤1}RHom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ)^∨[−1] ≃ τ_{≤1}RHom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}Ȟ, O_Δ), where (−)^∨ = RHom_{O_Δ}(−, O_Δ). When R is perfectoid, Hom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ) = 0, so that in degree 1 one obtains Ext^1_{O_Δ}(Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ), O_Δ) ≃ Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}Ȟ, O_Δ) and therefore Ext^1_{Δ_R}(M_Δ(H), Δ_R) ≃ M_Δ(Ȟ), expressing the compatibility of M_Δ with Cartier duality on finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over R.
items.locator: arXiv:1907.10525v4 (11 October 2022), Remark 5.1.7 (not in the published version)
items.note: The crystalline analogue is Berthelot–Breen–Messing Theorem 5.2.7. This remark is present in arXiv v4 and absent from the published version, which passes directly from Remark 5.6 to the discussion of the Breuil–Kisin case; it is the only place where the two versions differ in content, and it is recorded here so that the design job plans the duality statement.

items.name: Quasi-syntomic perfectoid covers of regular local rings
